title: Cranberry Sauce

drivers.name: Competitor store opening
drivers.evidence: A new competitor across the street may reduce demand; no past data confirms this, so effect is small and uncertain.

drivers.name: Price increase (2.1%)
drivers.evidence: Price rose slightly but no past promotion at this level shows demand lift; noise-adjusted promotion effects are near 1.0.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 9.0. A competitor opening across the street is a known demand-eroding event, but no prior evidence shows a consistent impact. The price increase to $2.91 (+2.1%) is modest and not linked to past demand shifts. The classical uplift model suggests +23% from Thanksgiving, but the target week is 6 weeks after Thanksgiving (2026-11-16), well beyond the typical spike window. Past Thanksgiving effects decay quickly, and no recent promotion or event supports lift. The noise-adjusted effect of Thanksgiving is already modest (x1.23), and the baseline has captured seasonal trend (trend_13_vs_prior_13_pct=55.6%). No driver justifies a multiplier above 1.0. Confidence is medium due to limited evidence on competitor impact.

PRODUCT: Cranberry Sauce | category Grocery | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-22 (6 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 2.91 (+2.1% vs regular price 2.85)
  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 9.0 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 20.6 | 10%-90%: 1.3 - 17.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-81% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
